sermon.title: The End Time Judgment, Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the final revelation in Revelation is the judgment of God, and that ministers must preach it because everyone will stand before Christ and be judged by their works. He covers the second death and lake of fire, the book of life, the sheep and goats of Matthew 25 and how we treat God’s people, and being ready to die.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he says “Isaiah 39:11” for the words about the day of the Lord, which are in Isaiah 13:9-11; he says “Revelations 2014” for Revelation 20:14 and “Psalms 15” for Psalm 1:5; the words are kept as spoken (with the reference corrected to Psalm 1:5 and Revelation 20:14 in the text). “David Kzer” in the captions was corrected to “David Kincer,” and several caption slips were corrected (“cure the least” to “care the least,” “fragrantly” to “flagrantly,” “life name” to “life maimed,” “Ofra” to “Oprah”). One spot is marked [unclear] (“wiz word”). His comments about named public figures, homosexuality, drugs, medical marijuana, “home Bible studies,” and the rapture are his own and are not verified here. The “purgatory” remark is sarcastic as spoken.

chunks.section_question: What are the three revelations in the book of Revelation, and why can’t John add to the word?
chunks.short_answer: He says there are three revelations in Revelation: the revelation of Jesus Christ, of His church, and of the judgment of God, “the same revelation that’s in the rest of the New Testament and the rest of the Old Testament.” He says John could not add to or take away from the word, so if something is not found in the rest of the scriptures “we’re missing the revelation of revelations.”
chunks.text: The end lesson of revelations is the end time judgment. I told you there were three revelations in revelations. First, it is the revelation of Jesus Christ. Wow. Jesus Christ. He knows it because he just taught it or he’d have forgot it too. The second revelation in Revelation is the revelation of his church. The third revelation is the revelation of the judgment of God. The same revelation that’s in the rest of the New Testament and the rest of the Old Testament. Same revelation. You see, John said, “You can’t add to the word or take away from it.” See, John could do nothing that didn’t already been spoken in the scriptures. And so when we go to Revelations and we take things out and twist it and make great fairy tales out of it, that’s not what John is doing.

chunks.section_question: What does the Bible say about the coming judgment? (Psalm 1:5, Psalm 98:9, Daniel 7:10, Daniel 12:2, Matthew 16:27, Acts 10:42)
chunks.short_answer: He gives scriptures that the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment, that the Lord will judge the world with righteousness, that the books were opened, and that the Son of Man will reward “every man according to his… works, his behavior, his action.” He says Jesus commanded the apostles “to preach to the people and to testify that it is Jesus who was ordained by God to judge,” and that “you’re going to be judged.”
chunks.text:
If it’s not found in the rest of the scriptures, we’re missing the revelation of revelations. Hallelujah. Did John have to keep his own principle, not adding to the word nor taking away? Absolutely. In fact, it wasn’t his words. It was Christ’s words he was given to. Hallelujah. Okay, I want to give you some scriptures about the judgment. Psalms 1:5, the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment. Psalms 98:9, the Lord is coming to judge the earth with righteousness. He will judge the world and the people, the flocks, the congregations with impartiality. Yes, you’re going to be judged. You’re quoting Jesus and believing in Jesus is not going to keep you from standing before Christ.

Isaiah 39:11, “The day of the Lord comes. It’s going to be a cruel day with both wrath and fierce anger, and he will destroy the sinners in it. For the stars of heaven and their constellations will not give light. The sun will be darkened. The moon will will not shine. And I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their iniquity. And I will stop the arrogance of the proud. That’s Old Testament stuff. Daniel 7:10. 10,000 times 10,000 stood before him, and the judgment seat was set, and the books were open. The book of works, the book of your actions, the book of your behavior is opened. Daniel 12:2, “Many that sleep in the dust of your of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, t some to shame and everlasting contempt.” Matthew 16:27, “The Son of man shall come with his angels.

He commanded us, the apostles, to preach to the people and to testify that it is Jesus who was ordained by God to judge, to be the judge of the living and of the dead.

chunks.section_question: Will believers escape the judgment because they believe in God? (Romans 2:3, 2 Corinthians 5:10)
chunks.short_answer: He says the judgment is “an eternal judgment” and that God “doesn’t judge by emotions. He judges by truth.” He says being a believer, being baptized, in a Christian church, or saying “I love Jesus” does not let you escape if you commit sin, and cites 2 Corinthians 5:10, that we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ to receive what we have done, “whether it be good or whether it be bad.”
chunks.text:
The judgment’s a serious thing. It’s an eternal judgment, folks. There’s no getting back out. Once the judgment is passed, there is no. And God isn’t like the judges today, as we’re going to see in this message. He doesn’t judge by emotions. He judges by truth. Hallelujah. This is a serious message. Romans 2:3. You who judge those practicing sinful things and you do the same. Do you think you’re going to escape the judgment of God? What is he saying? Because you’re a Jew and you believe in God and yet you’re doing what the sinners do. You think because you believe in God and you learned about God, that you’re going to escape the judgment just because you’ve accepted Christ and you’ve been baptized and you’re in a Christian church and you know, you say, “I love Jesus.” And yet you commit adultery.

You lie. You steal and flagrantly break the word out. You think you’re going to escape the judgment? No way. Now I’m giving you the scriptures. This is not David Kincer. This is the author of the Bible. And the only thing I have permission to teach is what he taught. I don’t have permission to give you my opinion. I can’t say I believe unless I’m believing what he believes. Are you there? And do you know you can’t do that either? You know, you’re saying, “Well, I don’t see nothing wrong with it. Doesn’t matter if you see what’s wrong with it.” What does God see? Hallelujah. The judgment is serious.

It’s very serious. Listen to this. 2 Corinthians 5:10. Parents, young people, you got to get this. 2 Corinthians 5:10. We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ. What made them, you know, do things where they were stoned and put in prison and beaten over and over?

chunks.section_question: Why are people who warn about the judgment mistreated? (2 Corinthians 5:11)
chunks.short_answer: He says the apostles suffered because “they understood that there’s a judgment to come and we got to persuade men to escape that judgment.” He says when you have that concern you may be mocked or separated from, because you are disturbing their comfort zone, and that churches start in unity around mercy but divide over “doctrines of discipline.”
chunks.text:
And what made them act like that and put up with that? Because they understood that there’s a judgment to come and we got to persuade men to escape that judgment. Yes. Yes. Give the Lord a clap offering for the [unclear] word. Yes. See, and when you get that concern, you’re going to be mistreated. You’re going to have people separate from your company. You’re going to have them mocking and laughing at you. Why? You are disturbing their comfort zone. And they don’t care if Jesus said it, if God said it.

They don’t want to hear it. Your family members can turn on you. Your friends can turn on you. Church members can turn on you. You see the church starts in unity around Jesus. We all like that message of mercy and forgiveness all of us. And then it starts dividing over other doctrine because people don’t want to embrace restraint doctrine, discipline, doctrines of discipline. And so they separate you and they laugh at you and they’ll call you a holy roller or a religious extremist or whatever. And all you’re doing is just expanding your faith in God’s word and exercising it and preaching it.

chunks.section_question: What is the second death, and will everyone be resurrected? (Revelation 20:14)
chunks.short_answer: He says everyone dies once, then “you’re going to be resurrected” whether you believe in it or not, and stand before the white throne to give an account. He says those who rejected Jesus’ word “You’re going to be cast into the lake of fire” as the second death, while those who repent and don’t flagrantly sin, “We’re only going to die once.”
chunks.text:
And the judgment is one of the top messages. Is that a good amen? And you young people, don’t you believe this nonsense from TV and what people are telling you. They’re telling you a bunch of lies. This Bible is the facts. This is the truth. It’s really going to happen. Now, the lake of fire, which is the second death. See, you die once and you go to the grave, young people. Then you’re going to be resurrected and ain’t a thing you can do about it. You don’t have any control over this. It’s going to happen whether you believe in it or not.

And you’re going to be resurrected. Your body is going to come back to you. It’s going to materialize. And you’re going to stand before his white throne before the judgment and give an account of your life. It’s going to happen. Okay. You are resurrected. You might be 14. You might be 24. You might be 54. You might be 68. You might be 99 when you die, but you’re going to be resurrected.

You’re going to die one time. And that’s all God intended for you to do is die one time. Physically die. But on that day, if your behavior wasn’t right, if you rejected Jesus, you say, “But I didn’t reject Jesus.” Yes. But see, Jesus said, “In works they disown me. With the mouth they profess to know me, but they don’t choose my word and live by my word.” So, that is a rejection of who? Jesus. See, you can’t separate Christ and his word. They’re the same. Isn’t that right? Yes. And then you’re going to die a second death. You’re going to be cast into the lake of fire. He said, “That’s the second death. You’re going to die twice. But those of us who live for God and we might make mistakes but not flagrant and we don’t flagrantly sin.

chunks.section_question: Who goes into the lake of fire, and how long does it last? (Revelation 19:20, Revelation 20:10, Revelation 20:14)
chunks.short_answer: He says the beast and the false prophet were cast alive into the lake of fire, then the devil, who is “tormented… forever,” and then death and hell. He says “the last enemy” is death, and that we already have Satan “under our feet.”

Do you young people understand that? This is serious stuff. Who’s going to go to the lake of fire? Revelations 19:20, the beast and the false prophet are cast alive into the lake of fire. They’re already there. The Devil Revelation 20:10 that deceived the nations was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone where the beast and beast and false prophet are already there. The first two to go was the beast and the false prophet and then Satan.

And they’re going to be tormented for a few days in purgatory and they can pray their way out. They’re going to be tormented how long, young people? Forever. Say it. Forever. Here forever. Revelations 20:14, death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. What’s the last enemy? What’s the last enemy? Death. See, that last enemy that God Jesus is going to destroy when he comes is death. See, we already have Satan under our feet. A lot of you don’t know that, but you do. If if I could just get it through your cranial vacuum, you are a powerful people. Death and hell were cast into the lake of fire.

See, when we confess our sins and ask him to come into our life, he forgives, he cleanses, and he because our past is erased by his blood. chunks.section_question: What is the judgment of the sheep and the goats about? (Matthew 25:31-46)
chunks.short_answer: He says that when the Son of Man comes, the nations are separated like sheep and goats, and those on the left are sent to everlasting fire for not feeding, clothing, visiting or taking in “the least of my brethren, the church, the Christian, the believer.” He says “how I treat the people of God is going to determine my destiny at the judgment.”
chunks.text:
All not found, written in the book of life, was cast into the lake of fire.” Now look at this one. And I want you adults attention here. When the Son of Man comes in his glory and all his holy angels with him, he will sit on the throne of his glory. All nations are going to be gathered together before him and he will separate them as a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats. And he’ll say to them on the left hand, okay, some went to the right, some went to the left. Those on the left. He says, “Depart from me, you cursed and to everlasting fire prepared for the Devil and his angels.” And then they say, “Well, Lord, when did we, you know, what do we do that we deserve this?” And he says, “Well, I was hungry and you didn’t feed me.

I was naked and you didn’t clothe me. I was in prison and you didn’t visit me. I was sick and you could care the least. I was a stranger and you wouldn’t take me in to your house and fellowship with me. He says, “Well, when did we see you?” He said, “When you didn’t do it to the least of my brethren, the church, the Christian, the believer. You didn’t do it to me. See, how I treat the people of God is going to determine my destiny at the judgment. Now, a lot of you think that this is only a natural illustration.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the holy angels with Him, then He will sit on the throne of His glory. All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them one from another, as a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats. And He will set the sheep on His right hand, but the goats on the left. Then the King will say to those on His right hand, ‘Come, you blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world: for I was hungry and you gave Me food; I was thirsty and you gave Me drink; I was a stranger and you took Me in; I was naked and you clothed Me; I was sick and you visited Me; I was in prison and you came to Me.’ “Then the righteous will answer Him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You drink? When did we see You a stranger and take You in, or naked and clothe You? Or when did we see You sick, or in prison, and come to You?’ And the King will answer and say to them, ‘Assuredly, I say to you, inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these My brethren, you did it to Me.’ “Then He will also say to those on the left hand, ‘Depart from Me, you cursed, into the everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels: for I was hungry and you gave Me no food; I was thirsty and you gave Me no drink; I was a stranger and you did not take Me in, naked and you did not clothe Me, sick and in prison and you did not visit Me.’ “Then they also will answer Him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to You?’ Then He will answer them, saying, ‘Assuredly, I say to you, inasmuch as you did not do it to one of the least of these, you did not do it to Me.’ And these will go away into everlasting punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

We just got religion.” He says we must feed them with the word.

chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus told Paul “you’re persecuting me” because “God sees the church as himself,” and Paul received correction. He cites Mark 9:43 and says Jesus is giving “a natural illustration of a spiritual” and wants us to cut the sin off, not our hands; he says he has dealt with people who tried to harm themselves over “this rapture thing.”
chunks.text:
But you see, if I can open your understanding, see, God sees the church as himself. And when Paul was mishandling the church, Jesus came to him to correct him. And Paul received correction. And God saved and became one of the the chiefest apostle. Amen. Lake of fire, second death. Those who do not repent and restrain from sin. Mark 9:43. If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better to enter into life maimed than to go to hell and into the fire that will never be quenched. That’s that second death. Now, he’s not telling you to cut off your hand and put out your eye like I’ve dealt with. I can’t believe people do. I just see he gives us a natural illustration of a spiritual. He wants us to cut the sin off.

I actually dealt with, you know, in these home Bible studies and these garage Bible studies, you know, geez. And especially this second coming extremism where they think they aren’t going to be able to make it tomorrow. So, my God, I got to do something to be ready. This rapture thing has destroyed a lot of people, I’m telling you. And I have to deal with it. And it’s sad when a young person comes to me and they try to there’s the scars where they try to literally cut off their hand and their eyes gone because they put out their eye. Geez. I mean, common sense tells you how you going to read the book if you put out your eyes. How you going to work and provide for yourself and your family if you got no hands?

chunks.section_question: Is God fair when young people die?
chunks.short_answer: He says some people die young, citing John the Baptist, the children in Bethlehem and Job’s children, and says “you don’t tell God he’s not fair.” He says God designed this and “has a destiny in mind, and he’s going to reach it,” and allowed Job’s trials to prove people would serve Him whether bad things happen or not.
chunks.text: But I’m a Christian. I don’t care. John the Baptist died at 33 because he stood up for the word. Are you there? Those children in Jerusalem or Bethlehem, I’m sorry, under two years old all died because Herod did not want a king living. And so he just killed every kid trying to get to Jesus. You say, “Well, that’s just not fair.” Listen, you don’t tell God he’s not fair. I don’t know what kind of mentality this world has given you, but our God has designed this thing, and he has a destiny in mind, and he’s going to reach it. And yes, he allowed Satan to kill Job’s children to prove to us and to the world that people would serve him whether bad things happen to them or not.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “For who has known the mind of the LORD? Or who has become His counselor?”

faqs.question: What does he call the main part of the gospel?
faqs.answer: He says telling people of the judgment is “the main part of the gospel,” coupled with the part that “we’re the bride of Christ and Jesus loves us and we can all know him.”

faqs.question: What does he say about approving of sin in others?
faqs.answer: He cites Romans 1:32 and says those who do such things deserve death “approve of those who practice them,” and that approving of sin means joining in the judgment. He lists homosexuality, adultery and stealing among the sins and also mentions drugs.

scriptures.text_nkjv: who, knowing the righteous judgment of God, that those who practice such things are deserving of death, not only do the same but also approve of those who practice them.

faqs.question: How does he say God judges?
faqs.answer: He says “he doesn’t judge by emotions. He judges by truth,” and that “once the judgment is passed, there is no” getting back out.

faqs.question: Why does he say he cannot give his own opinion?
faqs.answer: He says “the only thing I have permission to teach is what he taught,” the author of the Bible. He says “I can’t say I believe unless I’m believing what he believes,” and asks what God sees rather than what we think is wrong.

faqs.question: Why does he say works matter in rejecting Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus said that in works they disown Him, and with the mouth they profess to know Him but “don’t choose my word and live by my word.” He says “you can’t separate Christ and his word. They’re the same.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: They profess to know God, but in works they deny Him, being abominable, disobedient, and disqualified for every good work.

faqs.question: What does he say we already have over Satan?
faqs.answer: He says “we already have Satan under our feet,” and that the last enemy Jesus will destroy when He comes is death. He tells his listeners, “you are a powerful people.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: The last enemy that will be destroyed is death.

faqs.question: What does he say hell is and what is the second death?
faqs.answer: He says “hell is the abiding place of the dead that has gone on before,” and that the second death is being cast into the lake of fire for those whose names are not found in the book of life.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And anyone not found written in the Book of Life was cast into the lake of fire.

faqs.question: Does he say helping the poor is enough?
faqs.answer: He says we should still help, but “that is not the meat of this message.” He says people can feed the poor and help orphans “and not know God,” and that helping people in sin and weakness is more needed.

faqs.question: What does he draw from Lazarus being bound in grave clothes?
faqs.answer: He says baby Christians have a long way to go, and as Lazarus still wore grave clothes Jesus told His people to loose him. He says “God wants us involved” in helping people out of bondage.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And he who had died came out bound hand and foot with graveclothes, and his face was wrapped with a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Loose him, and let him go.”

faqs.question: What does he say about second-coming extremism?
faqs.answer: He says he has dealt with people who tried to cut off a hand or put out an eye because they feared they would not be ready for the rapture, and says “this rapture thing has destroyed a lot of people.” He says common sense tells you how you would work or read if you did that.

faqs.question: What did he learn about sickness and death?
faqs.answer: He says he was in the “faith camp” and fought with God about Christians dying healthy, but “the prophets died of sicknesses” and “death in the sight of God is a precious thing when you know him.” He says we were ordained to die because of the tree of knowledge of good and evil.

faqs.question: What does he tell young people?
faqs.answer: He says “be ready to die,” and that he has done funerals for teenagers after accidents and overdoses. He says “you got a promise of 70 to 80 years, but you got no guarantee of tomorrow.”
